{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-me-c","lineage":{"candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-me-class-c:lineage:44","input_manifest_sha256":"80a49e48e114223b4aba1e630eb1c30c7716691ded557f1c4ffb0a64cc36afd1","source_registry_sha256":"c2e42c38f9f4644827a2fdadadd6340aab123a85c208ecc4839848339c6c9a98","source_liveness_sha256":"e742bf2373c9a6bebd7774b2b45ae2a58ba395947586ea942f331e99a0744f40"},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C2"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C2","chunk_id":"C2.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"Sharing the Road","heading":"C2 — Sharing the Road","learner_facing":false,"markdown":"## C2 — Sharing the Road

FACT_ID: sec10-R01 | anchor: A105
Check mirrors and blind spots carefully for small, less visible motorcycles. [A105]
Source: [A105 -> pdf-0105]

FACT_ID: sec10-R02 | anchor: A105
Look ahead and to the sides before a left turn and wait for an oncoming motorcycle to pass. [A105]
Source: [A105 -> pdf-0105]

FACT_ID: sec10-R03 | anchor: A105
A flashing motorcycle turn signal may have been left on because it does not always cancel automatically. [A105]
Source: [A105 -> pdf-0105]

FACT_ID: sec10-R04 | anchor: A105
Leave at least a 4-second following gap behind a motorcycle and increase it when the road is wet. [A105]
Source: [A105 -> pdf-0105]

FACT_ID: sec10-R05 | anchor: A105
Expect a rider to change speed or lane position to avoid potholes, loose material, slick spots, seams or railway crossings. [A105]
Source: [A105 -> pdf-0105]

FACT_ID: sec10-R06 | anchor: A106
Large vehicles have extensive blind spots despite their mirrors, so avoid remaining in those areas. [A106]
Source: [A106 -> pdf-0106]

FACT_ID: sec10-R07 | anchor: A106
Never pass behind a reversing bus or truck. [A106]
Source: [A106 -> pdf-0106]

FACT_ID: sec10-R08 | anchor: A106
If a large vehicle’s mirrors are not visible to you, its driver probably cannot see you. [A106]
Source: [A106 -> pdf-0106]

FACT_ID: sec10-R09 | anchor: A106
Allow buses and trucks extra room for acceleration, braking and turning. [A106]
Source: [A106 -> pdf-0106]

FACT_ID: sec10-R10 | anchor: A106
A large vehicle can lose speed sharply uphill or gain it quickly downhill, so avoid taking away its operating space. [A106]
Source: [A106 -> pdf-0106]

FACT_ID: sec10-R11 | anchor: A106
When a large vehicle follows you, leave ample room ahead so both drivers have time to respond. [A106]
Source: [A106 -> pdf-0106]

FACT_ID: sec10-R12 | anchor: A106
Do not pull or pass in front of a large vehicle that is already slowing or stopping. [A106]
Source: [A106 -> pdf-0106]

FACT_ID: sec10-R13 | anchor: A106
A truck or bus may swing left before a right turn; watch its position and signals and stay clear of the turn path. [A106]
Source: [A106 -> pdf-0106]

FACT_ID: sec10-R14 | anchor: A107
No-Zones are large-vehicle blind areas at the front, rear and sides. [A107]
Source: [A107 -> pdf-0107]

FACT_ID: sec10-R15 | anchor: A107
The manual identifies a truck’s largest side blind area on its right, extending rearward from the cab. [A107]
Source: [A107 -> pdf-0107]

FACT_ID: sec10-R16 | anchor: A107
Avoid lingering beside a large vehicle because a sudden lane change or swerve can cause a collision. [A107]
Source: [A107 -> pdf-0107]

FACT_ID: sec10-R17 | anchor: A107
After passing a large vehicle, wait until its whole front is visible in your rearview mirror before returning to its lane. [A107]
Source: [A107 -> pdf-0107]

FACT_ID: sec10-R18 | anchor: A107
Do not tailgate a truck to draft in its wake; close following also blocks your view ahead. [A107]
Source: [A107 -> pdf-0107]

FACT_ID: sec10-R19 | anchor: A107
When stopped behind a large vehicle uphill, leave room for possible rollback as it starts. [A107]
Source: [A107 -> pdf-0107]

FACT_ID: sec10-R20 | anchor: A108
Wait until a large vehicle completes its turn before making a turn into its path. [A108]
Source: [A108 -> pdf-0108]

FACT_ID: sec10-R21 | anchor: A108
To reduce wind effects from an oncoming truck, use the rightmost portion of your own lane. [A108]
Source: [A108 -> pdf-0108]

FACT_ID: sec10-R22 | anchor: A108
If uncertain about an oncoming truck’s speed, wait for it to pass before turning left. [A108]
Source: [A108 -> pdf-0108]

FACT_ID: sec10-R23 | anchor: A108
Stop behind intersection stop lines so large vehicles have turning clearance. [A108]
Source: [A108 -> pdf-0108]

FACT_ID: sec10-R24 | anchor: A108
Do not cut ahead of a truck or race it into a construction section that narrows to one lane. [A108]
Source: [A108 -> pdf-0108]

FACT_ID: sec10-R25 | anchor: A108
Give large vehicles additional space on every side in bad weather or limited visibility. [A108]
Source: [A108 -> pdf-0108]

FACT_ID: sec10-R26 | anchor: A108
On slick roads, avoid maneuvers that force a bus or truck to brake unnecessarily. [A108]
Source: [A108 -> pdf-0108]

FACT_ID: sec10-R27 | anchor: A108
Following a large vehicle too closely both hides you from its driver and limits your view of the road. [A108]
Source: [A108 -> pdf-0108]

FACT_ID: sec10-R28 | anchor: A109
Dim headlights when following a large vehicle at night to avoid glare in its mirrors. [A109]
Source: [A109 -> pdf-0109]

FACT_ID: sec10-R29 | anchor: A109
Before passing a large vehicle, inspect ahead, behind and the side you intend to move toward. [A109]
Source: [A109 -> pdf-0109]

FACT_ID: sec10-R30 | anchor: A109
Pass a large vehicle only in a legal passing area and only when the maneuver can be completed without speeding. [A109]
Source: [A109 -> pdf-0109]

FACT_ID: sec10-R31 | anchor: A109
Check over your shoulder before returning to the right lane after passing a bus or truck. [A109]
Source: [A109 -> pdf-0109]

FACT_ID: sec10-R32 | anchor: A109
If a large vehicle passes you, stay to the right within your lane until it clears and maintain speed or ease off slightly. [A109]
Source: [A109 -> pdf-0109]

FACT_ID: sec10-R33 | anchor: A109
On wet roads, start the wipers before a passing large vehicle throws spray across your view. [A109]
Source: [A109 -> pdf-0109]

FACT_ID: sec10-R34 | anchor: A109
Yield to an emergency vehicle using flashing lights and a siren by pulling to the road edge and stopping. [A109]
Source: [A109 -> pdf-0109]

FACT_ID: sec10-R35 | anchor: A109
Clear an intersection before pulling aside for an emergency vehicle; do not block the intersection. [A109]
Source: [A109 -> pdf-0109]

FACT_ID: sec10-R36 | anchor: A109
Do not follow a fire truck responding to an alarm within 500 feet. [A109]
Source: [A109 -> pdf-0109]

FACT_ID: sec10-R37 | anchor: A110
For a police stop, pull to a safe place on the right and remain inside unless asked to leave the vehicle. [A110] [A109]
Source: [A110 -> pdf-0110]

FACT_ID: sec10-R38 | anchor: A110
During a police stop, shut off the engine, switch on hazard flashers and open the window for communication. [A110] [A109]
Source: [A110 -> pdf-0110]

FACT_ID: sec10-R39 | anchor: A110
At a night police stop, switch on the interior light so the officer can see inside. [A110] [A109]
Source: [A110 -> pdf-0110]

FACT_ID: sec10-R40 | anchor: A110
Stay calm and keep seat belts fastened during a traffic stop, including those of passengers. [A110] [A109]
Source: [A110 -> pdf-0110]

FACT_ID: sec10-R41 | anchor: A110
Keep hands on the steering wheel during a traffic stop. [A110] [A109]
Source: [A110 -> pdf-0110]

FACT_ID: sec10-R42 | anchor: A110
If an officer requests license, insurance or registration, explain where it is and reach slowly while keeping one hand on the wheel. [A110] [A109]
Source: [A110 -> pdf-0110]

FACT_ID: sec10-R43 | anchor: A110
Do not try to flee a traffic stop. [A110] [A109]
Source: [A110 -> pdf-0110]

FACT_ID: sec10-R44 | anchor: A110
For an emergency vehicle stopped at the roadside, slow and yield; change into the next lane when possible and safe. [A110]
Source: [A110 -> pdf-0110]

FACT_ID: sec10-R45 | anchor: A110
If moving over is unsafe, slow down and pass the stopped emergency vehicle cautiously. [A110]
Source: [A110 -> pdf-0110]

FACT_ID: sec10-R46 | anchor: A110
The rear orange-and-red reflective or fluorescent triangle identifies a vehicle traveling below 25 mph. [A110]
Source: [A110 -> pdf-0110]

FACT_ID: sec10-R47 | anchor: A110
Approach a slow-moving vehicle cautiously and pass only after confirming it is safe. [A110]
Source: [A110 -> pdf-0110]

FACT_ID: sec10-R48 | anchor: A111
Watch for farm equipment crossing rural roads or using highways, and pass carefully because its operator may not see or hear you. [A111]
Source: [A111 -> pdf-0111]

FACT_ID: sec10-R49 | anchor: A111
Slow and pass animals or animal-drawn vehicles cautiously because a startled animal may rear, swerve or stop. [A111]
Source: [A111 -> pdf-0111]

FACT_ID: sec10-R50 | anchor: A111
Horse riders and horse-drawn vehicles share the road and follow vehicle traffic rules. [A111]
Source: [A111 -> pdf-0111]

FACT_ID: sec10-R51 | anchor: A111
Avoid using the horn or revving the engine near an animal, and never deliberately frighten an animal ridden, driven or led near a public way. [A111]
Source: [A111 -> pdf-0111]

FACT_ID: sec10-R52 | anchor: A111
Watch for animal-drawn traffic turning left into a field or driveway and heed signs warning of that traffic. [A111]
Source: [A111 -> pdf-0111]
